title: Vision Encoders & Alignment
description: Study image patches and spatial information, contrastive image-text learning, projection and cross-attention interfaces, and grounding and spatial evaluation. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Image patches and spatial information
lessons.description: Calculate the patch count at 448 by 448 and explain the consequence for attention memory.
lessons.conceptOverview: A vision transformer splits an image into patches and embeds each patch with position information. Smaller patches retain finer detail but produce more tokens; preprocessing resolution changes both detail and cost.
lessons.whyItMatters: Resolution must be budgeted in tokens as well as pixels.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A vision transformer splits an image into patches and embeds each patch with position information. Smaller patches retain finer detail but produce more tokens; preprocessing resolution changes both detail and cost.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: A vision transformer splits an image into patches and embeds each patch with position information. Smaller patches retain finer detail but produce more tokens; preprocessing resolution changes both detail and cost.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A 224 by 224 image with 16 by 16 patches yields 196 patch tokens before special tokens. Doubling each image dimension produces four times as many patches.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Calculate the patch count at 448 by 448 and explain the consequence for attention memory. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Resolution must be budgeted in tokens as well as pixels.
commonMistakes: Doubling image width and height only doubles the patch count.

lessons.title: Contrastive image-text learning
lessons.description: Design a validation set with swapped backgrounds and captions that distinguish the products.
lessons.conceptOverview: Contrastive training brings paired image and text representations together while separating competing pairs. Success depends on pair quality and negatives; shared proximity reflects training associations rather than a guarantee of factual recognition.
lessons.whyItMatters: Counterexamples can expose shortcuts in image-text alignment.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Contrastive training brings paired image and text representations together while separating competing pairs. Success depends on pair quality and negatives; shared proximity reflects training associations rather than a guarantee of factual recognition.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Contrastive training brings paired image and text representations together while separating competing pairs. Success depends on pair quality and negatives; shared proximity reflects training associations rather than a guarantee of factual recognition.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Two product images share the same background and near-identical captions. A model can learn the background shortcut instead of the distinguishing product feature.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Design a validation set with swapped backgrounds and captions that distinguish the products. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Counterexamples can expose shortcuts in image-text alignment.
commonMistakes: High training similarity proves the model recognizes the intended object.

lessons.title: Projection and cross-attention interfaces
lessons.description: Draw the encoder, adapter and decoder boundaries and identify where resolution loss occurs.
lessons.conceptOverview: A language model needs an interface to visual features. Projection maps features into compatible dimensions; cross-attention lets text states attend to visual states. Training the interface alone saves resources but limits what can adapt.
lessons.whyItMatters: An adapter cannot reliably reconstruct visual details discarded upstream.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: A language model needs an interface to visual features. Projection maps features into compatible dimensions; cross-attention lets text states attend to visual states. Training the interface alone saves resources but limits what can adapt.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A frozen image encoder misses tiny serial numbers. Enlarging the language-side projection cannot recover information absent from the image features.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Draw the encoder, adapter and decoder boundaries and identify where resolution loss occurs. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: An adapter cannot reliably reconstruct visual details discarded upstream.
commonMistakes: A larger projection always repairs inadequate image resolution.

lessons.title: Grounding and spatial evaluation
lessons.description: Create separate identification and localization acceptance checks for five crowded images.
lessons.conceptOverview: Grounding associates a phrase with a region rather than merely describing the whole image. Bounding-box overlap measures localization, while phrase accuracy measures identification; one metric cannot replace the other.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluate the region and its label separately.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A system names the correct valve but highlights its neighbor. Caption accuracy is high while the localization needed by a technician is wrong.
